data.one_liner: Official Flutter plugin for authenticating users and requesting OAuth scopes via Google Sign-In.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter apps to authenticate users using their Google accounts across Android, iOS, macOS, and Web. Handles lightweight sign-in, explicit authentication UI flows, and separate OAuth authorization for Google APIs. Provides access tokens and server auth codes for backend verification.
use_when: Your application needs to allow users to sign in with their Google account.
You need OAuth access tokens or server auth codes to call Google APIs on behalf of the user.
avoid_when: You only need local device biometrics or PIN authentication without Google accounts.
You are targeting Windows or Linux desktop platforms where this plugin is not supported.
strengths: Official Flutter plugin supporting Android, iOS, macOS, and Web.
Decouples basic authentication from authorization, matching modern OAuth security standards.
Supports lightweight silent sign-in and streaming authentication state events.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific setup and integration steps for each target OS.
Web platform has specific constraints, such as mandatory SDK-rendered buttons and non-refreshing access tokens.
data.setup_notes: Requires client ID configuration and separate native setup across Android, iOS/macOS, and Web.

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you want a complete identity platform supporting multiple providers (email, Google, Apple) alongside backend auth state management.

alternatives.name: local_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you need device-level biometric or passcode checks rather than federated Google account sign-in.
